text:
Chen Tingfei Leads in Tainan Mayoral Race, New Poll Reveals
A recent poll indicates Chen Tingfei currently holds a significant advantage in the race for Tainan mayor, sparking accusations of strategic alliances and raising concerns about interference in the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) primary. The survey data suggests a challenging path forward for Lin Junxian, whose campaign is questioning the integrity of the competition.
The latest data, released Thursday, shows Chen Tingfei with a commanding lead within the green camp, while Lin Junxian trails with just 3% support.
Accusations of Blue Camp Collaboration
The Lin Junxian campaign has alleged that Chen Tingfei is engaged in a “selfish alliance” with members of the Kuomintang (KMT), specifically naming MPs Cai Yuhui and Chen Tingfei. These accusations center on the possibility of coordinated strategies designed to weaken the DPP’s overall position in the upcoming mayoral election.
“We are deeply concerned about the potential for outside influence in this primary,” a senior campaign official stated. “The suggestion that our opponent is collaborating with members of the opposing party is a serious matter that demands a full investigation.”
Cai Yuhui and Chen Tingfei have both responded to the allegations, denying any improper collaboration.
KMT Intervention and DPP Concerns
The controversy extends beyond the internal DPP dynamics, with Progressive Party members voicing criticism of the KMT for allegedly intervening in the primary process. These members believe the KMT is actively attempting to influence the outcome to favor a candidate they perceive as weaker in the general election.
“The KMT’s attempts to meddle in our internal affairs are unacceptable,” one party member commented. “They are clearly trying to manipulate the situation to their advantage, and we must resist their efforts.”
Expert Predictions and the Road Ahead
Political analysts predict a fierce battle within the green camp, but remain skeptical of Lin Junxian’s chances. Guo Zhengliang forecasts that Lin Junxian will likely lose the election, citing the current polling data and the strength of Chen Tingfei’s campaign.
The situation highlights a growing divide within the DPP, with some members advocating for a “clean” primary focused on internal strengths, while others express concerns about the potential for external interference. The outcome of this primary will undoubtedly shape the future of Tainan’s political landscape and could have broader implications for the DPP’s performance in future elections.
